# Host prompt contract

The plugin is an OpenCode `LanguageModelV3` provider (`aisdk:antigravity`), so
OpenCode calls `doStream` in-process and owns the agent loop. For primary
Antigravity requests, the `context` session hook writes the active agent's
`system` field and OpenCode's instruction sources into provider options; the
adapter forwards both and drops OpenCode's assembled system message. Instruction
sources include AGENTS.md files, generated skills, MCP guidance and project
references; OpenCode's date and environment are omitted because the ACP harness
supplies its own. A missing, empty or whitespace-only field means no
instructions; agent lookup failures propagate instead of falling back.

The adapter sends a nonempty agent prompt and instructions as one text block:

```xml
<instruction>
Configured agent system prompt, unchanged.

OpenCode instruction sources, unchanged.
</instruction>
```

User content follows without a `[user]` marker or adapter boilerplate. The
plugin preserves OpenCode's new-child subagent introduction. It never adds
that introduction itself, so continuation messages are not prefixed again.
Conversation history, attachments and original tool results remain available
when continuing or rebuilding a trajectory. Changed/cleared instructions
retire the previous ACP context, including a parked tool turn once its results
are available, so old instructions are not silently retained.

ACP initialization omits optional `clientInfo` and advertises empty
`clientCapabilities`. Tool configuration uses the protocol's `mcpServers`
field with a server named `external_tool`; model selection is unchanged.

These rules govern the host input to ACP, not Antigravity's own internal
system prompt/metadata. Auxiliary title/generate requests keep their dedicated
utility behavior. Compaction also runs as an isolated summary turn: its result
lets the host rewrite history, and the next primary request reseeds a fresh ACP
session from that rewritten history. This does not promise to resolve Google
location restrictions.

# OpenCode Antigravity

An OpenCode V2 plugin that exposes Google's Antigravity ACP agent as an
`antigravity` provider. OpenCode owns the agent loop and calls the in-process
AI SDK `LanguageModelV3` adapter; the adapter starts a separately installed
ACP server and bridges OpenCode tools to it. This is not an Anthropic HTTP
proxy and is not an official Google or OpenCode product.

## Requirements and setup

1. Use an OpenCode V2 host compatible with the plugin API used here
   (`@opencode/plugin` 2.0.22). The package requires Bun >= 1.4.4 and exports
   TypeScript source; the OpenCode host must provide Bun.
2. Obtain Google's **ACP Registry 1.5.2 Linux x64** standalone artifact from
   the [`antigravity-acp` entry in the official Registry manifest](https://cdn.agentclientprotocol.com/registry/v1/latest/registry.json)
   and extract it. The manifest is a moving latest listing; check the version
   before downloading. This project does not install the
   artifact. Keep `agy_acp_server.par` and `localharness_external` together.
   The launcher must be executable. The adapter admits only Linux x64 and
   checks the SHA-256 of **both** extracted files before launching:

   | File | SHA-256 |
   | --- | --- |
   | `agy_acp_server.par` | `f472860b79c4816a32817e589afdb01cec0ca731e5fa428eae873b14be12387f` |
   | `localharness_external` | `072fc497e7814b0e25a7d80109bceddacd815eb351d2e48ce579a05510e0cfdf` |

   For example, run `sha256sum agy_acp_server.par localharness_external` in
   the extracted directory. These pins are an admission check, not an
   automatic download or update mechanism. See
   [the migration notes](docs/agy-cli-migration.md) for the artifact review.
3. Sign in separately with the official `agy` CLI using a personal account.
   The CLI is used for its existing personal authentication, **not** as the
   ACP runtime. The plugin does not initiate interactive login. It reads the
   CLI token file at `$GEMINI_HOME/antigravity-cli/antigravity-oauth-token`
   (default `$HOME/.gemini/antigravity-cli/antigravity-oauth-token`) and stages
   a translated credential in an account-scoped private profile. Protect that
   profile and never share credentials or its contents. The plugin does not
   modify the CLI token or reuse an existing standalone credential.
4. Set `OPENCODE_ANTIGRAVITY_ACP_PATH` to the full path of the extracted
   `agy_acp_server.par` in the environment of the OpenCode **server**; or put
   the pair together in a directory on its `PATH`. An explicit path is the
   launcher, not its directory or the `agy` CLI. A long-running shared service
   must actually inherit the chosen environment.
5. Install dependencies in this checkout using Bun:

   ```sh
   bun install --frozen-lockfile
   ```

   Add the **absolute path to this checkout directory** to your global
   `~/.config/opencode/opencode.jsonc` or a project's `opencode.jsonc`,
   preserving any existing configuration. Replace the example path:

   ```jsonc
   {
     "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
     "plugins": ["/absolute/path/to/opencode-antigrvity"]
   }
   ```

   See the OpenCode
   [plugin guide](https://opencode.ai/docs/build/plugins) and
   [configuration guide](https://opencode.ai/docs/config). The npm latest
   release 0.6.5 predates this runtime; publication of 0.6.6 has not been
   verified. Use the current checkout for the behavior documented here. The
   plugin registers the provider and a
   non-secret local connection marker automatically; no Google API key needs
   to be configured in OpenCode.

Use `/models` in OpenCode to select an available **Antigravity** model after
discovery. Model
IDs and availability come from the authenticated ACP session, not a fixed
list in this repository; before successful discovery the fallback catalog is
empty. Some explicitly advertised effort siblings are grouped into variants
(`low`, `medium`, `high`). Availability can change by account or runtime.
Unknown model limits are estimates, not guarantees.

## Tools, prompts, and safety

OpenCode tools are presented to ACP through an `external_tool` MCP bridge;
OpenCode continues to own tool execution and permissions. The reviewed
standalone runtime is configured with an empty native-tool allowlist. Do not
substitute the CLI-embedded `agy acp` or an unreviewed binary: an isolation
test of CLI 1.5.18 found native tool access despite the requested disabling
flag. This is a specific reviewed runtime boundary, not a general sandbox or a
guarantee against all server behavior. Native ACP permission requests default
to deny; `OPENCODE_ANTIGRAVITY_ACP_PERMISSION=allow` changes that policy and
should only be used with an understanding of the risk. See
[migration notes](docs/agy-cli-migration.md).

OpenCode agent instructions and instruction sources are forwarded to ACP;
the harness supplies its own internal system context. See the
[prompt contract](docs/prompt-contract.md) for history, subagents and
compaction. The adapter ignores temperature overrides; ACP owns sampling.
Text and image input and text output are advertised, subject to the actual
runtime and model. Usage may fall back to an approximate context occupancy
when ACP does not report usage; it is not billing accounting. See
[development notes](docs/development.md#usage-fallback) for limitations,
including tool-bridge changes and session reconstruction.

The adapter stores session state and private profiles under
`OPENCODE_ANTIGRAVITY_DATA_DIR`, or by default under
`${XDG_DATA_HOME:-~/.local/share}/opencode-antigravity`. Durable OS locks live
separately in the OS account home. Stop all old adapter processes before an
upgrade across the lock-protocol boundary; do not delete lock files while
processes are running. See [lock recovery](docs/lock-recovery.md).

## Troubleshooting

- **Executable not found or rejected:** check the server environment, execute
  permission, platform, exact filename, companion location and both hashes.
  An explicit `OPENCODE_ANTIGRAVITY_ACP_PATH` disables `PATH` fallback, even
  if the override is invalid. Symlinks are resolved before admission: the real
  launcher's basename must be `agy_acp_server.par`, with the matching
  `localharness_external` next to that real file.
  The CLI-embedded ACP, other versions and other platforms are not admitted.
- **Authentication required:** sign in through `agy` separately with personal
  authentication and ensure the server sees the same `HOME`/`GEMINI_HOME`.
  Do not paste or print token contents into logs or issue reports.
- **No models / unknown model:** check authentication and runtime discovery;
  the empty fallback does not invent models. Select an ID actually advertised
  by the session. Account access, quota and service availability remain
  external dependencies.
- **Lock or session recovery issues:** consult [lock recovery](docs/lock-recovery.md)
  before manual cleanup. For host problems, see OpenCode's
  [troubleshooting guide](https://opencode.ai/docs/troubleshooting); redact
  credentials, prompts and private data before sharing diagnostics.

## Development and tests

```sh
bun install --frozen-lockfile
mkdir -p /tmp/opencode
bun run check                 # build and test suite
bun test test/protocol.test.ts # one test file
```

`bun run build` type-checks source and emits `dist/`; the default suite uses
fixtures and skips live tests when not enabled. `bun run test:live` opts into
real inference and may consume quota; it requires the admitted runtime and
existing authentication. See [development](docs/development.md) for details;
historical baseline counts and platform reviews in the docs are not a promise
of current support. Never commit credentials or local environment files.

# Antigravity ACP 1.5 migration

The supported runtime is Google's **ACP Registry 1.5.2 Linux x64** executable and its matching `localharness_external`. Both files are verified against pinned executable hashes. The ZIP was verified against the official ACP Registry manifest. Set `OPENCODE_ANTIGRAVITY_ACP_PATH` to the extracted `agy_acp_server.par`, or place both files together on `PATH`. There is no 1.3 fallback.

This is not the CLI-embedded `agy acp` runtime. CLI 1.5.18 failed the native tool A/B test: with no MCP servers and `disableBuiltInTools: true`, it called a native tool and read a sentinel file. The registry runtime supports `_meta.antigravity.enabledTools: []`; its embedded source applies the filter in agent construction and restores it on resume. Live tests through this adapter verified that both fresh and resumed sessions refused to read a sentinel file with no MCP servers, with zero tool events. A separate adapter inference smoke test returned its expected marker.

Sign in through `agy`. The adapter reads the personal CLI refresh credential from `$GEMINI_HOME/antigravity-cli/antigravity-oauth-token` (default `$HOME/.gemini`), translates it into the standalone server's format, and writes it only into an account-scoped private profile. It does not modify the CLI credential, use a pre-existing standalone credential, or start interactive login. Missing CLI credentials fail before ACP starts. Unsupported binaries and platforms are rejected.

# Windows CLI credential review

Reviewed the official CLI 1.3.5 Windows x64 artifact linked by the install
service's `manifests/windows_amd64.json` on 2026-10-14:
`https://storage.googleapis.com/antigravity-public/antigravity-cli/1.3.5-6164039479459840/windows-x64/cli_windows_x64.exe`.
SHA-512 (matches that manifest):
`4483cac360dcedcdba19c49d4e589559ce7fcba039daf1887ffa5bd68d1f4437660733295822c13283d4243e00813259ad839466f5b9bc6c20728077a392d38c`.

The Go function table identifies zalando/go-keyring's `windowsKeychain.Get`
and `.Set`, and `codeassistclient.KeyringTokenStorage.LoadStoredToken`.
The latter reads keyring service `gemini`, converts the returned string to
bytes (`runtime.stringtoslicebyte`), and calls `encoding/json/v2.Unmarshal`
into `codeassistclient.StoredToken`. Runtime struct metadata gives its
`token` and `auth_method,omitempty` JSON fields. It also includes unrelated
ID token, WIF, project, region and tier fields which this adapter ignores.
The upstream go-keyring v0.2.6 Windows implementation uses target
`service + ":" + username`, reads `string(cred.CredentialBlob)` and writes
`[]byte(password)`. The reporter independently identified the exact generic
target `gemini:antigravity`. Thus the supported envelope is UTF-8 JSON, not
Credential Manager's sometimes-used UTF-16 password representation.

The adapter reads only that target via CredReadW, frees its native buffer,
bounds blob/output size and execution time, and suppresses all native error
details. A custom HOME or GEMINI_HOME remains file-only. It never creates a
CLI token file, starts login, enumerates credentials, or writes the keyring.
Native CI uses synthetic credentials on a disposable GitHub runner only.

# macOS ARM64 isolation review

Downloaded the official ACP 1.3.0 Darwin ARM64 archive and independently
verified both profile SHA-256 values. Extracted ZIP local entries from the
PAR executable (without executing it):
`google3/cloud/developer_experience/antigravity_extensions/acp_server/tool_filter.py`
and `server.py`. `ToolFilterConfig.from_request_kwargs` reads
`_meta.agy.enabledTools`; an empty list becomes an empty tuple, not None.
`resolve_disabled_builtins` disables everything outside that allowlist.
`_create_agent_config` applies that result, excludes the safe_view_file
substitute, and gates subagents and browser injection. Session creation,
restoration and agent rebuild all pass/persist the filter. This is a static
host-tool isolation review; native unauthenticated startup CI does not prove
authenticated inference.

# Development

## Prerequisites

- Bun >=1.4.4. The repository pins Bun 1.4.4 in `package.json` and CI; update
  both pins together.

Use Bun for installs, scripts, builds, tests, and CI. `bun.lock` is the sole
lockfile; do not create or update locks with another package manager. CI uses
`bun ci` (equivalent to `bun install --frozen-lockfile`): it verifies the lock
is current and installs its exact versions. For local development, the frozen
install is equally reproducible.

```sh
bun install --frozen-lockfile
mkdir -p /tmp/opencode
bun run check
```

## Daily workflow

Edit TypeScript in `src/` and add regression tests in `test/`.

```sh
bun run build                     # Type-check and emit dist/ declarations and JS
bun test test                     # Run tests without rebuilding
bun test test/protocol.test.ts     # Run one test file
bun test --watch test              # Re-run tests as files change
bun run --bun tsc -p tsconfig.json --watch # Run TypeScript under Bun while watching
bun run check                     # Build and full tests before submitting changes
```

This repository is a plugin/library, not a standalone development server.
The package entrypoint is `src/index.ts`; generated output lives in the ignored
`dist/` directory. The build type-checks `src/`, not the test files.
The OpenCode host must provide Bun at runtime. Imports from `node:` in source
and tests use Bun's Node.js API compatibility layer; they do not launch or
require the Node executable. TypeScript and the fake ACP test executable are
explicitly run with Bun. `@types/node` remains only to type-check those
compatible APIs; it does not add a Node runtime requirement.

Bun skips dependency lifecycle scripts unless a package is explicitly trusted.
Do not trust dependencies broadly: Koffi's optional platform package supplies
its prebuilt native binary, so its Node-based install script is intentionally
left untrusted. A clean Bun install and Koffi import were verified on Linux.

## Usage fallback

Tool-enabled native sessions rebuild from host history when their MCP bridge
endpoint changes, including after bridge recreation. The execution profile
stores a hash, not the endpoint token. Do not resume across a changed endpoint
until the admitted standalone runtime is verified to replace its MCP wiring;
reconstruction must not re-execute historical tool calls. Tool-free sessions
can still resume when their history and settings align.

ACP prompt-response usage is authoritative when present, including explicit
zero values. If it is absent, the language model may report a fresh measured
context occupancy as input tokens with zero output tokens. This is an
approximation of the current context, not per-request token accounting or
billing usage.
Fallback measurements stay bound to the response receipt and execution
generation. A turn without a new sample may reuse the latest measurement from
that same generation for up to five minutes, rechecked when each new terminal
or tool response is emitted. Completed receipt replays retain their original
response payload. A replacement execution cannot inherit the previous
generation's occupancy.

## Optional live tests

The default suite uses fixtures and skips opt-in live and platform-specific
checks when their prerequisites are unavailable. Normal development does not
require Google credentials or a running Antigravity server.

`bun run test:live` enables real inference checks. Only run it after configuring
the official Antigravity ACP executable and authentication; it may consume
account quota. See `test/acp-live.test.ts` and `src/acp-detect.ts` for the checks
and executable discovery behavior. Do not commit credentials or local `.env`
files.

## Verified baseline

Setup was verified with Bun 1.4.4: the build succeeded, with 212 tests passing,
10 skipped, and no failures. The provider registers through OpenCode's
`LanguageModelV3` AI SDK hook (`aisdk:antigravity`); there is no loopback HTTP
proxy or Anthropic Messages emulation.

A prior lockfile audit reported 4 dependency vulnerabilities (1 moderate,
3 high). Dependency upgrades were deliberately left out of this migration;
some remediation changes the pinned OpenCode plugin version and needs separate
compatibility testing.

# Durable lock recovery

The adapter now acquires locks with the operating system instead of PID files:
POSIX `flock` on Linux/macOS and `LockFileEx` on Windows. The native handle is
held by the server process, so the OS releases ownership when that process
exits or is killed. If the native library or OS call is unavailable, locking
fails closed; there is no lease, token-unlink, or unlocked fallback.

Native lock files are persistent and live in the OS account home namespace at
`<account-home>/.local/share/opencode-antigravity/.locks/`. The account home is
resolved from the OS user record, not from `HOME`, `XDG_DATA_HOME`, or
`OPENCODE_ANTIGRAVITY_DATA_DIR`, so environment overrides cannot split
ownership. Lock names use canonical physical resource paths, allowing
processes with different session-store directories to rendezvous on a shared
installation. These files are outside temporary utility directories that
retention can remove. Do not delete or move the namespace while any adapter
process is running. The lock protocol is intended for processes sharing a
local filesystem with working OS advisory-lock semantics; it is not a
distributed lock service.

## Upgrade boundary

Stop every OpenCode server, desktop service, and other process using the same
adapter data directory before upgrading. The previous PID/reaper protocol and
the native OS-lock protocol are **not rolling-upgrade compatible**: an old
process does not honor the new native lock, so it could otherwise overlap a
new server on an unmarked resource.

At startup, the new version checks old lock files and `.reap` chains. It removes
them only when every encountered owner has a recognized PID and that PID is
definitely gone. Live, permission-protected, malformed, or otherwise unknown
owners are left untouched and block that resource. If the adapter reports an
older or unknown lock owner, stop all old servers first and retry. If an
unknown record remains after shutdown, preserve the data directory and
investigate it before any manual cleanup; the adapter will not guess that it
is safe to delete.

Historical deletion-temp files are swept separately, without acquiring the
session-store lock. Only the exact old `<sha256>.json.<pid>.<uuid>.tmp` format
with a definitely dead PID is removed. Active or unrecognized files remain
untouched. New atomic writes use four serialized staging slots per destination,
so failed cleanup cannot grow the number of staging files without bound.
